root_cause_label: Incomplete Cancellation Handling for Queued Tasks
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent implemented concurrency limiting with asyncio.gather and Semaphore but held a false premise that this pattern correctly propagates cancellation to tasks queued behind the semaphore, never testing the cancellation-above-max-concurrent scenario that the grader evaluates.
t_err_evidence: Step 3: agent creates run.py using asyncio.gather with asyncio.Semaphore. The wrap pattern does not ensure cleanup runs for tasks still waiting to acquire the semaphore when cancellation occurs; the agent's plan already assumed 'asyncio.gather will propagate CancelledError to each wrapped task — that's fine' without verifying this covers the queued case.
t_commit_evidence: Step 5: agent revisits run.py and explicitly reasons 'The current implementation should be fine' for the cancellation requirement, then rewrites the file while retaining the same flawed asyncio.gather pattern. This locks in the wrong implementation; no further attempt is made to change the core logic.
trigger_explanation: The agent assumed asyncio.gather automatically ensures cleanup code runs in all tasks, including those still blocked waiting to acquire the semaphore. In practice, tasks that have not yet started (i.e., still waiting on semaphore.acquire) receive CancelledError but may not execute their try/finally cleanup logic in all scenarios, particularly for the test_tasks_cancel_above_max_concurrent case. The agent never verified this assumption.
